arguments.text: Fixed. `Interval.fromISO` was parsing both halves as DateTimes up front; with `throwOnInvalid = true`, `DateTime.fromISO("PT5H30M")` threw before the duration fallback could run. Each half is now parsed in a try/catch so a throwing parse is treated as invalid and the code falls through to `Duration.fromISO`. Both `"2020-06-22T17:30:00.000+02:00/PT5H30M"` and the reversed form now return the same intervals as with the default setting; genuinely malformed input still throws. Lint passes and no pre-existing green tests broke (the 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures are unchanged).

arguments.text: Fixed. In `src/impl/util.js`, `objToLocalTS` built the timestamp with `Date.UTC(year, ...)`, which treats years 0–99 as 19XX, then "reverted" it by subtracting 1900 from the resulting year. That revert happened after the day rollover was computed, so a day overflow past Feb was resolved using the wrong leap-year rule (2000 is leap, 100 is not), landing on 0100-03-01 instead of 0100-03-02. It now re-sets the full year/month/day via `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`, so the rollover is computed with the real year's leap status. `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ day: 61 })` now yields 0100-03-02. Lint passes and no pre-existing green tests broke (the 2 pre-existing `toFormat` locale failures are unchanged).
